pr_title: Make universe data accessible via security object
pr_body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
This change adds the universe data to the security cache which can be accessed via `Security.Cache.GetData<T>` where `T` is the type of data.  `Security.Fundamentals` is a new property that provides a merged via of the coarse and fine data.

#### Related Issue
<!--- This project only accepts pull requests related to open issues -->
<!--- If suggesting a new feature or change, please discuss it in an issue first -->
<!--- If fixing a bug, there should be an issue describing it with steps to reproduce -->
<!--- Please link to the issue here: -->
Closes #1901 

#### Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
Many algorithms require access to the universe data to make decisions other than simply selecting the universe of securities. This change makes this data accessible.

#### Requires Documentation Change
<!--- Please indicate if these changes will require updates to documentation, and if so, specify what changes are required -->
Yes -- https://github.com/QuantConnect/Documentation/issues/57

<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->

issue_context.title: Add universe data to security object
issue_context.body:
<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Description
Currently the only way the algorithm can get access to the universe data (such as coarse/fine) is through the universe selection functions. Many algorithms require access to this data for other purposes. We need to make this data accessible via the security object and also provide a helper for the most common case of accessing the fundamental data, other universe data should be accessible via the security cache.

review_comments: Tried pretty hard to consolidate how we manage fine to be just like every other universe to no avail. This code is [smelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_smell) but works. Despite the stench factor, it actually made the merge operation below a breeze (otherwise it would have probably been implemented in the `Security.Fundamentals` property getter by combining the coarse/fine at invocation time.
idk about everyone else, but I'm a big fan of counting **all** of the data points :grin:
